smell_validity.evidence: Five flows absorb bodies of helpers that remain live and used elsewhere (tests import create_csr, ntlm_negotiate, get_crl): packaging guard and password policy copied into both forge.py and cert.py, writer body twice in cert.py, CMC wrappers and issued-cert handling into req.py, NTLMv2 computation into ntlm.py. Orchestration silently re-implements protocol and crypto rules; the double-ownership cost is unmistakable.

maintenance_impact.evidence: The copies force co-maintenance: identical packaging guard and encryption policy in two flows, the write body twice, NTLM and CMC construction duplicated, so a library fix silently misses flow copies, as the prompt's near-miss illustrates. Restoring calls re-establishes single ownership of crypto/protocol rules. Lasting trap, strongly beneficial, though package-scoped rather than architectural.

development_plausibility.evidence: Absorbed code is the project's own library logic, re-bound to flow state with matching terminology, imports and docstrings, so it sits naturally beside surrounding work. But inlining roughly 500 lines of CMC/CMS assembly across five flows at once, each with a parallel 'readable in one place' justification note, exceeds believable single-developer organic drift.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: It names the idiom (copied live-helper bodies), the finished state (flows call still-existing helpers, flow-specific edits stay around the call), hard exclusions (helpers never removed, byte-identical NTLM, PFX policy, tests stay green, no behavior change) and warns against stopping at the first long function — decisively blocking wrong direction, incomplete cleanup and irrelevant redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Distinct purposes need distinct code-supported decisions: file loading with three-tier error ladders, PEM/DER fallback chains, PFX packaging, three CMC wrapper flavors (signer identity and content type differ), attribute assembly, issued-cert reporting, template flag/capability derivation, NTLM negotiate versus proof/channel-binding computation. Decisions include DER-versus-object inputs, tuple return unpacking, flag-before-policy ordering and hex nthash conversion.

localization_burden.evidence: The prompt names domains, not files; each inline stretch must be matched to its helper across the commands/lib boundary (certipy flows duplicate certificate.py and ntlm.py helpers whose imports req.py dropped). cert.py's parameter aliases (file_path, password, data bound from options) must be seen through, and genuine locations such as req.py's remaining create_pfx call must be excluded.

repair_coordination.evidence: forge.py and cert.py copies share one packaging rule: reverting only one leaves a private encryption policy that future create_pfx changes never reach. In req.py the restored wrappers must preserve the csr_der pipeline's shared type contracts (archival takes an object, renewal raw bytes); a mismatch digests wrong content, surfacing only as malformed requests rather than local errors.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: The direct uniform rule — replace each copied stretch with a call to its helper — needs per-site input mapping (option aliases, self attributes, tuple returns, DER/object conversion) and fails where flow routing interleaves absorbed fragments (req.py wrapper flavors, find.py loop). The strongest single-helper rule, restoring create_pfx, covers only two of roughly thirty sites.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Two hidden failure paths: wrong argument or type restoration inside Request.request (nthash not hex-decoded, wrapper arguments swapped) and byte-level mistakes in the NTLM retry flow. The shipped tests exercise the helpers and the find/cert/forge flows, but no test drives the enrollment or retry flows, so such wrong repairs stay green and silent.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
